subject: Post-call: ClearPay concurrency profile + Redwood quota options
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Voss <evoss@clearpay.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: ClearPay concurrency profile + Redwood quota options

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and a few asks so we can put together a firm pilot quote and capacity plan. Short summary:

- Goal: Run real-time payment verification pipeline (tokenization + risk scoring + contextual enrichment) with streaming results to your checkout service.
- Primary SLOs you called out: p95 inference latency <= 150ms (end-to-end per-request), sustained throughput ~6k reqs/min, peak burst up to ~18k reqs/min for 2-3 minutes around promos, and per-session parallelism (up to 6 concurrent model calls per user session).
- Streaming: ~30% of requests are streaming (partial tokens returned while scoring continues).
- Authentication/hosting: prefer Redwood Dedicated in us-west for data locality; team also asked about VPC Private deployment for PCI scoping (we'll detail next).

Actionable asks for ClearPay so we can size concurrency & draft ratecard:
1) Can you confirm average and 95th percentile of simultaneous open sockets from a single checkout instance during peak? (example: 220 sockets per instance)
2) Typical ratio of long-lived sessions (websocket) vs. short HTTP connections during peak traffic?
3) A small sample trace (1 hour) with timestamped request counts by minute would help us tune batching and burst windows.

Attached: 'clearpay_conn_matrix.xlsx' (template — please fill the columns in the first sheet: instance_id, avg_sockets, peak_sockets, avg_parallel_calls, pct_streaming) and 'redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf' (draft rate tiers + dedicated/pilot options).

Proposed near-term pilot: 2-week pilot with Dedicated pool sized for 2k sustained concurrent connections with a 2x burst window for 3-minute intervals. This is preliminary until we get the data above.

Next steps: please fill the matrix and send sample trace; I'll have Marissa produce an initial pricing + SLA note once we get those numbers.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0189

Attachment: redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf (pdf, 180KB)

From: Elena Voss <evoss@clearpay.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: ClearPay concurrency profile + Redwood quota options

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the summary and the template. Quick answers below and I've attached a gzipped CSV of the 1-hour trace.

> 1) Simultaneous open sockets per checkout instance
We run on autoscaled checkout instances (K8s). Typical: 180-230 sockets per instance at peak; 95th: ~270.

> 2) Ratio long-lived websocket vs short HTTP
Around 25-30% long-lived websocket (checkout sessions that keep a socket open for progressive updates), rest are short HTTP calls.

> 3) Sample trace
Attached: clearpay_trace_20280415.csv.gz (1 hour, minute-granularity). The peak minute hit 19,400 requests across the fleet, sustained window ~6,200 r/min for 12 minutes.

Notes: during marketing promos we see brief surges where a single region spikes ~3x baseline for 2-4 minutes. We prefer not to degrade the user-visible streaming sessions — losing partial tokens impacts checkout UX.

Questions for you:
- For the 'per-session parallelism' do you recommend limiting per-session calls to avoid KV cache thrash?
- What fallback do you recommend if Dedicated pool is saturated (e.g., spill to hosted model with higher latency)?

Thanks,
Elena Voss
Head of Payments Engineering | ClearPay
evoss@clearpay.io

---
Attachment: clearpay_trace_20280415.csv.gz (gzipped csv, 45KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Voss <evoss@clearpay.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: ClearPay concurrency profile + Redwood quota options

Thanks Elena — that's extremely helpful and lines up with our rough expectations. A couple of notes from infra/price perspective and a proposed pilot configuration: 

Quoted for context:
On Wed, Apr 17, 2028 at 9:05 AM Elena Voss <evoss@clearpay.io> wrote:
> We run on autoscaled checkout instances (K8s). Typical: 180-230 sockets per instance at peak; 95th: ~270.
> Around 25-30% long-lived websocket (checkout sessions that keep a socket open for progressive updates)... peak minute hit 19,400 requests across the fleet, sustained window ~6,200 r/min for 12 minutes.

Redwood sizing suggestion (pilot):
- Dedicated pool in us-west: target capacity to support 2,500 sustained concurrent requests, with burst headroom to 7,500 reqs/min for 3-minute windows. This covers your 6.2k sustained and gives ~20% buffer.
- Concurrency controls: we recommend capping per-session parallel calls at 6 (your current observation). If you can reduce to 4 calls/session for streaming paths we can significantly reduce overall concurrent KV cache pressure (we can help with a small SDK change to multiplex some sub-requests).
- Streaming handling: Redwood supports multiplexed streaming sessions — we'll pin those to higher-priority threads and enable prefix KV caching for identical early-context tokens (helps p95).
- Fallback policy: primary is Dedicated; secondary is Hosted API (same model family but higher quantized latency ~250-300ms p95). We can configure an automatic spillover policy by region and by queue depth.

Pricing and credits: based on the pilot sizing above, I'm attaching a sanitized draft ratecard and a one-time pilot credit to offset overage during promo windows. See attached ratecard for per-token & per-connection calculations.

Action items and owners:
- Elena: confirm you can limit per-session parallelism to 6 (or trial 4 for streaming) — please update the conn_matrix. (ELENA)
- Marcus: prepare a pilot quote and an SLA appendix for Dedicated pool (MARCUS)
- Ben: prepare a short runbook for the spillover behavior and emergency throttles (BEN)
- Redwood: we'll provision a small test pool for a short smoke test once we have the filled matrix + trace.

Next meeting: propose Wed 2028-04-24 10am PT to review the filled matrix and the pilot quote.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
